CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFGRIDROW

CFGRIDROW fills a CFGRID by hand instead of from a query. Each tag adds one row; its DATA values go into the grid's CFGRIDCOLUMN columns in order.

Category

Forms

Syntax

<CFGRIDROW DATA="value1, value2, ...">

Attributes

DATA
Required. Comma-separated list of the row's values, one per CFGRIDCOLUMN, in column order.

Usage

CFGRIDROW is only used when the grid has no QUERY attribute, and it needs CFGRIDCOLUMN tags to name the columns. Because DATA is a comma-delimited list, a value cannot contain a comma.

CFGRIDROW may sit inside a CFLOOP within the grid, which is a handy way to show computed values.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- How long does a 1 MB download take? (1 MB = 8,388,608 bits) --->
<H3>The 1999 download calculator</H3>
<CFFORM NAME="Calc" ACTION="cfgridrow.cfm">
<CFGRID NAME="Speeds" WIDTH="360">
  <CFGRIDCOLUMN NAME="Line" HEADER="Connection">
  <CFGRIDCOLUMN NAME="Bps" HEADER="Bits/second" DATAALIGN="Right">
  <CFGRIDCOLUMN NAME="Minutes" HEADER="Minutes per MB" DATAALIGN="Right">
  <CFLOOP LIST="14.4K modem:14400|28.8K modem:28800|56K modem:53000|ISDN:128000|T1:1544000"
      DELIMITERS="|" INDEX="Line">
    <CFSET Bps = ListLast(Line, ":")>
    <CFGRIDROW DATA="#ListFirst(Line, ':')#,#Bps#,#DecimalFormat(8388608 / Bps / 60)#">
  </CFLOOP>
</CFGRID>
</CFFORM>
